note: Wednesday 07:00 SGT sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Tue 21 Jul US close — levels/quotes are as of that close unless noted. Fresh items are dated 21-22 Jul. Every item source-verified (dates, numbers, attributions checked against the cited pages).

items.headline: Silver rips ~4% to ~$59 Tuesday, biggest up-day in weeks, as risk-on rebound lifts the whole complex
items.summary: COMEX/spot silver surged ~4.1-4.5% Tuesday to ~$59.0-59.2/oz, sharply outperforming a firm gold as the broad market snapped a three-day losing streak and metals caught a strong momentum bid. The move retraces most of last week's slide back toward the low-$56 area and puts silver back within ~50% of its late-January record near $121. Gold rose ~1.3-1.75% to ~$4,066-4,083.
items.actionable: A powerful relief rally for the levered silver sleeve — the $55.5-56 line held and the metal is back above $58. But the driver is risk appetite, not a rates thaw: the oil-led higher-for-longer Fed backdrop into the 28-29 Jul FOMC is intact, so treat this as a bounce to de-risk into, not confirmation of a new leg — keep leverage sized to survive another sharp reversal.

items.headline: Semis-led rally: S&P +0.89% to 7,509, Nasdaq +1.29% to 25,837; Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%, AMD +8%
items.summary: US stocks broke a three-day losing streak Tuesday as a memory-chip surge revived the AI-capex trade. Micron jumped ~12% and Sandisk ~14% on memory strength, and AMD added ~8% extending gains from its Microsoft AI deal. The S&P closed +0.89% at 7,509.20, the Nasdaq +1.29% at 25,837.21, the Dow +0.74% at 52,224.64. Of ~66 S&P names reported, ~88% have beaten EPS estimates. 10-yr yield ~4.63%.
items.actionable: The semis bounce is a direct positive read-through for HK-tech beta (SMIC 0981, Hua Hong) and the Tencent book. It relieves last week's SOX washout, but it's earnings-contingent — watch whether megacap AI results this week confirm the capex story before assuming the chip drawdown is over.

items.headline: Bitcoin hits a five-week high ~$66.5k as risk appetite returns; ETH and SOL firm
items.summary: Bitcoin rose to a five-week high, opening ~$65,214 Tuesday and trading up to ~$66,400-66,500 (+~0.8% on the day) as risk sentiment improved alongside the tech-led equity rally. ETH modestly outperformed and SOL firmed off its recent lows. BTC remains well below the Oct-2025 ATH (~$126k) but is reclaiming ground lost during the metals/semis selloff.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but BTC's five-week high confirms the risk-on turn that lifted silver and HK-tech — a useful confirming barometer. A sustained hold above ~$66k keeps the risk backdrop constructive; a failure back under ~$62.5k would be the early risk-off tell if Iran/Fed news sours.

items.headline: US strikes Iran for a 10th straight night; 10-day ceasefire proposal on the table, Houthis blockade Saudi, tankers hit near Hormuz
items.summary: The US ran a 10th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian command centers, missile/drone sites and air defenses. Qatar, Egypt, Pakistan and other mediators presented the US and Iran a 10-day ceasefire proposal. Meanwhile Yemen's Houthis declared an immediate naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, two Greek-managed tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz, and weekly Hormuz transits fell ~66%. Brent settled ~$89.2.
items.actionable: A firm oil bid supports the energy sleeve, but the biggest swing for the whole book is the ceasefire headline: a deal would deflate the Fed-hike premium that has pressured silver, gold, semis and HK tech — while a blockade escalation would spike oil and harden higher-for-longer. Trade the de-escalation risk, not the individual metals.

items.headline: Lynas reports June-quarter results Wednesday 22 July — the ex-China rare-earth bellwether
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths (LYC.AX) reports its June-quarter (Q4 FY26) production/sales update Wednesday. The stock has run ~63% over three months on the China export-curb re-rate and is not on China's control list (unlike MP Materials and USA Rare Earth, added 22 June). Its H1 FY26 showed record sales (~A$414m) and net income ~A$80m on Mt Weld expansion; new interim CEO Pol Le Roux took over 1 July.
items.actionable: The relative winner of the rare-earth watchlist reports today — watch NdPr output and pricing for read-through to the whole basket. After a ~63% run, a good print may already be discounted (sell-the-news risk); a miss would hit the ex-China names harder than the China-incumbent counter-bet 6680.HK. Treat the basket as event-driven and chop-prone.

items.headline: Alibaba rallies hard in HK ahead of earnings; Apple Intelligence clears China with Qwen as the model
items.summary: Alibaba (9988.HK) shares surged (as much as ~12% intraday earlier in the week, up again Tuesday) on pre-earnings optimism after reports of narrowing losses, with the stock near HK$117. Apple Intelligence obtained Chinese regulatory approval in mid-July with Alibaba's Qwen designated the foundational model for the localized experience. Tencent (0700) and Chinese AI names have ridden the same domestic-AI enthusiasm and Beijing's market-support push.
items.actionable: Direct tailwind for the Tencent/HK-China tech book: the Qwen-Apple deal is a concrete monetization signal for Alibaba's AI stack, and the whole complex has the 'national team' put beneath it. Watch Alibaba's actual earnings for confirmation; the swing factor remains fiscal follow-through at the late-July Politburo.

items.headline: Fed set to hold 28-29 July (~85%+); Warsh keeps higher-for-longer, market prices zero 2026 cuts
items.summary: Prediction markets put the probability of a hold at the 28-29 July FOMC above 85%, with roughly 76% odds of zero cuts in all of 2026 and only ~20% odds of even one 25bp cut. New Chair Kevin Warsh has kept a higher-for-longer stance, and the June SEP pencils PCE ending 2026 at ~3.6% (vs 2.7% prior). The oil surge has kept some hike risk alive for September.
items.actionable: The dominant macro headwind for the book's highest-beta pain point (levered silver + gold miners) and for SG REITs remains higher-for-longer with hike risk, not cuts. Silver's Tuesday rip is a risk-on bounce, not a rates thaw — the FOMC/statement next week is the key event. The big cash pile still earns ~3.6-4% as productive dry powder for pullbacks.

items.headline: Brent holds ~$89-90 as Hormuz risk premium persists; gasoline elevated
items.summary: Brent traded ~$89.9/bbl Tuesday morning, ~$1.71 above the prior day and roughly $20 above year-ago levels, as the Houthi Saudi blockade, tanker strikes near Hormuz and the ~66% drop in strait transits kept a firm risk premium in crude despite the ceasefire proposal. WTI held the low-$80s. US pump prices remain roughly a third above pre-war levels.
items.actionable: Sticky $80s-90s oil is a double edge: bullish for the energy sleeve and the inflation-hedge thesis, but it feeds the Fed's higher-for-longer stance that pressures gold, levered silver and rate-sensitive S-REITs. The ceasefire proposal is the key de-escalation watch that would relieve both oil and the rate-hike premium.

items.headline: Gold rebounds ~1.3-1.75% back above $4,060 as the risk-on bid finally reaches the metal
items.summary: Gold rose ~1.3-1.75% Tuesday to ~$4,066-4,083/oz, its first firm up-day in over a week, joining the broad risk rally and lifting off the $4,000 shelf it had defended near nine-month lows. Silver still outpaced it (~4%), but the bounce eases the immediate pressure on the gold-miner sleeve. The metal remains rangebound below its spring highs as real rates stay the dominant driver.
items.actionable: $4,000 held and gold is back above $4,060 — relief for GDX (down ~12% YTD toward ~$71-72 support). But this is a bounce within a rates-driven correction; the FOMC next week is the arbiter. A clean reclaim of ~$4,150 would signal the miners' washout is done; a fade back to $4,000 keeps them on watch.

items.headline: Three S-REITs — Keppel DC REIT, Suntec, Mapletree Industrial — report Thursday 23 July
items.summary: The first real test of the S-REIT sleeve this season lands Thursday. Keppel DC REIT is the strongest set-up: last DPU S$0.02833 (+13.2% YoY), distributable income +20.7% to S$74.6m, leverage 35.1% and ~51% rental reversion. Suntec's last DPU was S$0.01936 (+23.9% YoY) on thin NPI growth; Mapletree Industrial Trust is the laggard with full-year DPU S$0.1271 (-6.3% YoY) and leverage near ~37.5%.
items.actionable: Expect dispersion, not a sector move — Keppel DC's data-centre momentum is the bull case, MIT's shrinking DPU the warning. Check which of the three you hold before Thursday; higher-for-longer rates from the oil shock are a headwind for the whole S-REIT complex.

items.headline: DBS crosses S$200B market cap (first SGX company ever); Singtel running a S$2B buyback
items.summary: DBS (D05) became the first SGX-listed company to cross S$200B market cap on 13 July, and Singtel (Z74) launched a S$2B buyback on 9 July, underscoring aggressive capital return by Singapore blue-chips. SGX small/mid-caps roughly doubled the STI's 1H-2026 return, and industrial S-REITs yielding above 6% remain the income focus into a higher-for-longer backdrop. The STI is consolidating just below its ~5,561 record.
items.actionable: Constructive backdrop for the SGX bank/REIT sleeve: DBS and Singtel are returning capital aggressively, a support under the blue-chip book. The consolidation off records is war/tech jitters, not a bank-specific problem — no action needed unless the STI breaks the ~5,400 area.

items.headline: Uranium holds ~$86/lb; miners still weak despite structural deficit and hyperscaler nuclear deals
items.summary: Spot U3O8 was ~$85.7/lb as of mid-July, consolidating in an $84-87 band after January's spike above $101. Miners and ETFs (CCJ, UUUU ~$13.8, URA ~$43.2) remain in near-term downtrends even as hyperscaler nuclear procurement (Meta, Amazon, Microsoft) and a widening supply gap support the long-term bull case. Energy Fuels' $725M Pentagon loan remains the sector's marquee US-policy catalyst.
items.actionable: Weak tape, strong fundamentals — the uranium slice of the watchlist is catalyst-light near term and hostage to broad risk appetite. UUUU's dual uranium+rare-earth policy support is the multi-quarter call; the risk-on turn helps at the margin but don't expect leadership until it broadens.
